name: Las Vegas Sands
description: Las Vegas Sands develops and operates integrated resorts in Asia — combining casino gaming with hotel rooms, convention/MICE space, retail malls and dining. Since selling its Las Vegas Strip real estate and operations in 2022, the company's revenue base is entirely Macau (five properties under Sands China) and Singapore (Marina Bay Sands). It earns money on the house edge from table games and slots, room revenue, food & beverage, mall rent from retail tenants, and convention/entertainment fees. Marina Bay Sands, operating in Singapore's tightly-limited two-operator market, has become the company's single largest profit contributor, generating a majority of adjusted property EBITDA. The Macau business operates under a concession from the Macau government that runs through 2033 and carries mandated non-gaming investment commitments.

businessLines.name: Marina Bay Sands (Singapore)

share.text: approx. 40% of consolidated net revenue; approx. 56% of consolidated adjusted property EBITDA

businessLines.description: Single integrated resort in Singapore with casino, ~2,600 hotel rooms, convention center, retail mall (The Shoppes) and the rooftop SkyPark; benefits from Singapore's duopoly gaming license structure (only one other operator, Genting's Resorts World Sentosa).

businessLines.name: Macao properties (The Venetian Macao, The Londoner Macao, The Parisian Macao, The Plaza Macao & Four Seasons, Sands Macao)

share.text: approx. 52% of consolidated net revenue; approx. 44% of consolidated adjusted property EBITDA

businessLines.description: Five integrated resorts on the Cotai Strip and Macau peninsula operated by majority-owned subsidiary Sands China, combining mass-market and premium mass baccarat/table games, slots, hotel rooms across multiple brands, retail malls and MICE facilities under a Macau government gaming concession running through 2033.
